name: Ephemerid
concept: Post-RCE persistence-and-recovery demo kit for the lab: after execution on an allowlisted lab host, Ephemerid plants a clearly-labeled, marker-tagged persistence mechanism chosen from a menu (cron/systemd-timer, scheduled task / Windows Run key, service registration, webhook-at-boot) and then runs the recovery half of the loop — scanning the host for its own markers and common persistence footholds, driving a verification checklist that proves every artifact it planted, and finally executing a state-wipe kill-switch that removes all created artifacts and emits an evidence-of-cleanup report. A reversible, self-inventorying persistence cycle where detection and removal are first-class outputs.
attack_vectors: Linux: cron / systemd-timer backdoor launcher tagged with lab-UUID marker
Windows: scheduled-task + startup-folder / Run-key registration (winreg, stdlib)
Service registration: systemd unit / sc.exe-style service re-launching the beacon
Boot/webhook trigger: at-boot or webhook-fired re-arming channel (demo-only, logs every fire)
Recovery loop: marker scanner enumerates own artifacts + common footholds, cleanup checklist, state-wipe kill-switch and post-clean evidence report
novelty_angle: Persistence R&D usually optimizes stealth and lingering; Ephemerid inverts it — the implant is deliberately loud and label-tagged so the product is the self-detection + forensic-inventory + reversible-cleanup loop. Demonstrates realistic persistence mechanics while proving a complete state-wipe, so defenders learn what artifacts to hunt and operators get lab-safe removal practice without resembling a stealthy implant.
dependencies: posix where needed: crontab/systemctl on lab Linux host; winreg on lab Windows host
SSH/exec channel to lab host (stdlib subprocess/ssh; optional paramiko)
user-supplied lab CIDR in allowlist config
temporary disposable lab VM/container as victim
scope_gate: Central allowlist parser validates every host/path/CIDR against loopback + RFC1918 + user-supplied lab CIDR and refuses anything else; WARN banner with scope printout on first run; all planted artifacts embed a per-engagement lab-UUID so the recovery scanner only cleans hosts carrying that marker; cleanup report lists every artifact and asserts zero survivors before kill-switch self-destructs the tool's own working dir.
